A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Paper Copilot study, with complete main text and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, figures, tables and equations; differences are confined to the acknowledgment and version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original ICLR review analyses, a 1,860-response disclosure-consent survey in Section 4.1, and LLM metadata-extraction results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ICLR analyses, disclosure-consent survey and Appendix C extraction results, including Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The collection, normalization and versioning pipeline in Section 3, temporal review tracking in Section 4.1, and LLM metadata-extraction procedure in Appendix C are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain the ICLR 2017–2025 analysis, 2024/2025 rebuttal comparisons, four-conference consent survey, and the same eight venue rows and year ranges in Table 2.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same evaluated models: glm-4-plus, glm-4-air, glm-4-flash and glm-3-turbo. Appendix C also retains the cost-based exclusion of glm-4.

E3.justification: Samples and evaluation procedures are unchanged, including score binning, the score-combination frequency cutoff of 30, reviewer min–max differences, and Appendix C's structural-mismatch and success metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same confidence/rating analyses, score-footprint case example and ICLR 2024–2025 comparison. No ablations, robustness checks or supplementary analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changes to uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including 1,115 of 1,860 disclosure consents (59.9%), the 54.8% rating-update finding, and glm-4-plus's 86.82% success rate in Table 1. Appendix plots and Table 2 values are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical decision-entropy, logarithmic-scaling and ordered-logit expressions. Appendix C's tuple, mismatch and success-rate definitions are unchanged; no proofs or formal results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution statements and conclusion are unchanged, preserving claims about the tracking platform, review archive and 2025 shift toward sharper score-driven decisions.

C2.justification: Sections 5–7 and Appendix B retain the same interpretations of tiering, rebuttals and consensus, together with the same qualifications concerning voluntary sampling, privacy, misuse, bias and metadata accuracy.

D1.justification: The system stack, JSON records, dataset/code access information, token and cost disclosures, and Appendix A.2 reproducibility commitments are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work, citations and bibliography are identical. The paper's relationship to earlier datasets, review platforms and bibliometric systems is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 8 adopts collective acknowledgments and replaces explicit statements of full self-funding and independence from institutional/advisor backing with primarily personal effort/resources and a supportive advisor environment. The version/date stamp changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–2 retain identical displays, captions, axes, legends, formatting and placement. Page organization is preserved; the acknowledgment rewrite only reflows prose within its existing location.

improvement.justification: v2 revises the acknowledgment's voice and description of project support, plus the version/date stamp. Methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, reproducibility information and appendix material remain identical. These localized editorial changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
